segments.narration: An AI nearly doubled the number of drawings in this desert. Southern Peru, where the Nazca lines run for thirteen hundred kilometres.
They were made by scraping away the reddish pebbles to show the pale ground underneath. Most of the grooves are ten to fifteen centimetres deep.
Two thousand years of wind, almost no rain, and the hummingbird scraped into that plain is still sharp. So what were they actually for?
Not a star chart. Hawkins and Aveni tested the alignments and found the case too weak. The reading now is religious: paths walked in procession, and figures asking for water.
The 2024 survey confirmed 303 more, small relief figures sitting beside winding trails that lead toward the temple complex at Cahuachi.

verdicts.claim: A 2024 AI-assisted survey by Yamagata University and IBM Research confirmed 303 new figurative geoglyphs at Nazca, nearly doubling the number previously known, and the lines run more than 1,300 kilometres in southern Peru.
verdicts.note: 91% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 3 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The geoglyphs were made by removing the reddish iron-oxide-coated pebbles that cover the desert to expose the pale subsoil, and the lines are typically 10 to 15 centimetres deep.
verdicts.note: 81% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 2 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The Nazca lines were created between about 500 BC and AD 500 and survive because the local climate is dry and almost windless, with lime-rich subsoil that hardens in the morning mist.
verdicts.note: 78% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 1 number(s)

verdicts.claim: Gerald Hawkins and Anthony Aveni concluded in 1990 that the evidence for astronomical alignments was insufficient, and current readings treat the lines as ritual, including sacred pathways and figures invoking water.
verdicts.note: 67% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 1 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The 2024 study found the new relief-type figures clustered along winding paths associated with pilgrimage toward the Cahuachi ceremonial centre.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia links the 2024 reading of figurative geoglyphs to planned public architecture tied to pilgrimage and to the Cahuachi temples via Masini and Orefici. Press coverage of the same study describes the new figures as relief-type, smaller, and located close to winding paths, with the pilgrimage route running to Cahuachi.
